Thanks for taking this through. Attached are our redlines to the DPA (FinTechCorp_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx) and a short list of technical clarifications we need on the TOMs exhibit before we can route for internal sign-off:

- Cross-border transfers: we need explicit reference to SCCs + fallback to binding corporate rules; please confirm which mechanism Redwood intends to rely on for EU->US processing.

Marta —

Thanks for the redlines and the concise list. We're aligned on wanting this done quickly. High-level answers up front:

- Cross-border transfer mechanism: Redwood can support SCCs for the EU->US flow and will include contract language to fall back to SCCs if adequacy/other mechanisms change. We cannot accept BCRs on a one-off basis at this time.
- BYOK approach: we support two operational modes: 1) customer-managed keys wrapped with our HSM for key-use (no escrow), or 2) a limited escrow model where a customer key is split and stored in an HSM with strict access controls (legal request only, multi-person approval). Karthik, I'll let you add specifics.
- Rotation/revocation: revocation will cause new sessions to failover to a short-lived derived key path (we can provide a fallback re-encryption flow); expected service interruption in worst-case is the duration of a key rotation window (typically under 5 minutes for active sessions; persistent cached KV entries may require user-level replays).
- Audit evidence: monthly logs are feasible; we can provide timestamped access reports and a signed attest from our infra team for the first 12 months.

I'll route this to Karthik for a TOMs exhibit edit proposal and Monica for contract execution wording and eSign mechanics. Can we have a short 30-min call at 14:00 UTC today to walk the technical points?

Connor O'Brien
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Following the call, I attached a proposed TOMs exhibit (TOMs_Exhibit_ConnorsEdits_v1.pdf) that addresses Marta's bullet points. Key highlights:

1) Transfer mechanism: Exhibit 2.1 specifies SCCs as the primary lawful transfer mechanism and includes an automated routing clause that prefers EU-hosted processing for residency-sensitive workloads. We added: "Provider will notify Customer 60 days prior to any change in transfer mechanism and offer contract amendment options."

2) BYOK modes (section 4):
- Mode A (BYOK-wrapped): Customer uploads a key-encrypted key; Redwood stores only the wrapped-key inside our HSM. Redwood never has unwrapped key material.
- Mode B (Escrow-split): The customer's key is split via Shamir's Secret Sharing; one share is held in customer-managed KMS, one share in Redwood HSM. Release requires two-person approval and legal authorization for emergency access.

3) Rotation & revocation (section 5):
- Rotation cadence: configurable (30/90/180 days).
- Revocation behavior: active sessions derive ephemeral session keys; on revocation, new token issuance is blocked and existing token TTLs flush within a 5-minute window. We included a recommended customer runbook for re-keying long-lived artifacts.

4) Audit evidence (section 7): monthly signed access logs, HSM audit trail export (immutable append-only audit), and quarterly pen-test summary. We added a sample log schema.

I also redlined the DPA with minimal contract language to reference Exhibit 2 and 4. These are intentionally narrow edits to keep the main DPA intact.

Attachments: TOMs_Exhibit_ConnorsEdits_v1.pdf (pdf, 248KB), excerpt included below for quick visibility.

---Quoted excerpt---
Section 4.2 (BYOK-wrapped): "Provider will accept wrapped key material in PKCS#7 format encrypted with RSA-OAEP-256; unwrapping occurs only within FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSM enclaves. Provider retains only the wrapped form at rest."

Section 5.3 (Revocation): "Upon Customer revocation request, Provider will: (a) cease accepting new sessions using the revoked key within 5 minutes; (b) rotate derived session keys for active connections where feasible; (c) provide a revocation report within 4 hours."
